sanskrit.deva:
आविः संनिहितं गुहाचरं नाम महत्पदमत्रैतत्समर्पितम् ।
एजत्प्राणन्निमिषच्च यदेतज्जानथ सदसद्वरेण्यं परं विज्ञानाद्यद्वरिष्ठं प्रजानाम् ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
āviḥ saṃnihitaṃ guhācaraṃ nāma mahat padam atraitat samarpitam |
ejat prāṇan nimiṣac ca yad etaj jānatha sad asad vareṇyaṃ paraṃ vijñānād yad variṣṭhaṃ prajānām || 1 ||

lines.iast: āviḥ saṃnihitaṃ guhācaraṃ nāma mahat padam atraitat samarpitam
ejat prāṇan nimiṣac ca yad etaj jānatha sad asad vareṇyaṃ paraṃ vijñānād yad variṣṭhaṃ prajānām
lines.deva: एजत्प्राणन्निमिषच्च यदेतज्जानथ सदसद्वरेण्यं परं विज्ञानाद्यद्वरिष्ठं प्रजानाम्

padaccheda.iast: āviḥ saṃnihitam guhā-caram nāma mahat padam atra etat samarpitam ejat prāṇat nimiṣat ca yat etat jānatha sat-asat vareṇyam param vijñānāt yat variṣṭham prajānām
padaccheda.deva: आविः संनिहितम् गुहा-चरम् नाम महत् पदम् अत्र एतत् समर्पितम् एजत् प्राणत् निमिषत् च यत् एतत् जानथ सत्-असत् वरेण्यम् परम् विज्ञानात् यत् वरिष्ठम् प्रजानाम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Manifest, set close (in the heart), known as ‘moving in the cave’, is the great abode; in it all this is set: what moves, what breathes, what winks (and what does not). Know that, the formed and the formless, to be desired, beyond the knowledge of creatures, the best.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the khaṇḍa: how is the imperishable, which is without form, to be known?

Śaṅkara: āviḥ: shining forth. saṃnihitam: through the adjuncts, speech and the rest, it appears as if perceiving sound and the other objects (‘it blazes, it shines’, says another text); manifest through the properties of its adjuncts, seeing, hearing, thinking, knowing, it is perceived in the heart of all beings, set firmly there. guhācaram nāma: it is known as ‘moving in the cave’ because it moves there in the forms of seeing, hearing and the rest. mahat: being greater than all; padam: what is reached by all, the ground of all things. Why so great an abode: because in it all is set, as spokes in the hub of a wheel: what moves, birds and the like; what breathes, men, cattle and the like, with prāṇa and apāna; what winks; and, by ‘ca’, what does not wink.

Śaṅkara: jānatha: know this ground of all, pupils, as your own Self. sadasat: it is of the nature of being and non-being, the formed and the formless, gross and subtle, for apart from it they are not. vareṇyam: to be sought, for it alone, being eternal, is to be desired by all. paraṃ vijñānāt prajānām: beyond the knowledge of creatures, out of reach of worldly knowing. variṣṭham: best of all excellent things, for Brahman alone is free of every fault.

sanskrit.deva:
यदर्चिमद्यदणुभ्योऽणु च यस्मिंल्लोका निहिता लोकिनश्च ।
तदेतदक्षरं ब्रह्म स प्राणस्तदु वाङ्मनः ।
तदेतत्सत्यं तदमृतं तद्वेद्धव्यं सोम्य विद्धि ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yad arcimad yad aṇubhyo 'ṇu ca yasmiṃl lokā nihitā lokinaś ca |
tad etad akṣaraṃ brahma sa prāṇas tad u vāṅ manaḥ |
tad etat satyaṃ tad amṛtaṃ tad veddhavyaṃ somya viddhi || 2 ||

lines.iast: yad arcimad yad aṇubhyo 'ṇu ca yasmiṃl lokā nihitā lokinaś ca
tad etad akṣaraṃ brahma sa prāṇas tad u vāṅ manaḥ
tad etat satyaṃ tad amṛtaṃ tad veddhavyaṃ somya viddhi

padaccheda.iast: yat arcimat yat aṇubhyaḥ aṇu ca yasmin lokāḥ nihitāḥ lokinaḥ ca tat etat akṣaram brahma saḥ prāṇaḥ tat u vāk manaḥ tat etat satyam tat amṛtam tat veddhavyam somya viddhi
padaccheda.deva: यत् अर्चिमत् यत् अणुभ्यः अणु च यस्मिन् लोकाः निहिताः लोकिनः च तत् एतत् अक्षरम् ब्रह्म सः प्राणः तत् उ वाक् मनः तत् एतत् सत्यम् तत् अमृतम् तत् वेद्धव्यम् सोम्य विद्धि

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: That which is luminous, which is subtler than the subtle, in which the worlds and their dwellers are set: that is the imperishable Brahman; it is prāṇa, it is speech and mind (the consciousness within them). That is the true; it is immortal; it is to be pierced (by the mind): pierce it, dear one.

notes: Śaṅkara: arcimat: shining, for the sun and the rest shine by its light. Subtler than the subtle, than millet grains and the like; and, by ‘ca’, grosser than the gross, than the earth and the rest. In it the worlds, bhūḥ and the rest, are set, and their dwellers, men and the rest; for all are known to rest on consciousness. That ground of all is the imperishable Brahman; it is prāṇa, speech and mind, all the organs: that is, the consciousness within them, on which the whole aggregate of prāṇa and senses rests (‘the prāṇa of prāṇa’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.18). satyam: not false; so amṛtam, imperishable. veddhavyam: to be struck by the mind, that is, the mind is to be fixed in it. viddhi: fix your mind on the imperishable.

sanskrit.deva:
धनुर्गृहीत्वौपनिषदं महास्त्रं शरं ह्युपासानिशितं संदधीत ।
आयम्य तद्भावगतेन चेतसा लक्ष्यं तदेवाक्षरं सोम्य विद्धि ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dhanur gṛhītvaupaniṣadaṃ mahāstraṃ śaraṃ hy upāsāniśitaṃ saṃdadhīta |
āyamya tadbhāvagatena cetasā lakṣyaṃ tad evākṣaraṃ somya viddhi || 3 ||

lines.iast: dhanur gṛhītvaupaniṣadaṃ mahāstraṃ śaraṃ hy upāsāniśitaṃ saṃdadhīta
āyamya tadbhāvagatena cetasā lakṣyaṃ tad evākṣaraṃ somya viddhi
lines.deva: आयम्य तद्भावगतेन चेतसा लक्ष्यं तदेवाक्षरं सोम्य विद्धि

padaccheda.iast: dhanuḥ gṛhītvā aupaniṣadam mahā-astram śaram hi upāsā-niśitam saṃdadhīta āyamya tat-bhāva-gatena cetasā lakṣyam tat eva akṣaram somya viddhi
padaccheda.deva: धनुः गृहीत्वा औपनिषदम् महा-अस्त्रम् शरम् हि उपासा-निशितम् संदधीत आयम्य तत्-भाव-गतेन चेतसा लक्ष्यम् तत् एव अक्षरम् सोम्य विद्धि

translations.text: Taking the bow of the Upaniṣads, the great weapon, one should fit to it an arrow sharpened by meditation; drawing it with a mind absorbed in that (Brahman), pierce, dear one, that very imperishable as the mark.

notes: Śaṅkara: how it is to be pierced: taking the bow known from the Upaniṣads, the great weapon, one should fit to it an arrow sharpened, that is, refined, by constant meditation. āyamya: drawing it back, that is, withdrawing the inner organ together with the senses from its objects and turning it wholly to the mark; for here there is no drawing of a bow as with the hand. tadbhāvagatena: with a mind gone into the contemplation of that imperishable Brahman, the mark; pierce that very imperishable, as described, as the mark.

sanskrit.deva:
प्रणवो धनुः शरो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते ।
अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत्तन्मयो भवेत् ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
praṇavo dhanuḥ śaro hy ātmā brahma tal lakṣyam ucyate |
apramattena veddhavyaṃ śaravat tanmayo bhavet || 4 ||

lines.iast: praṇavo dhanuḥ śaro hy ātmā brahma tal lakṣyam ucyate
lines.deva: प्रणवो धनुः शरो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते

lines.iast: apramattena veddhavyaṃ śaravat tanmayo bhavet

padaccheda.iast: praṇavaḥ dhanuḥ śaraḥ hi ātmā brahma tat lakṣyam ucyate apramattena veddhavyam śaravat tanmayaḥ bhavet
padaccheda.deva: प्रणवः धनुः शरः हि आत्मा ब्रह्म तत् लक्ष्यम् उच्यते अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यम् शरवत् तन्मयः भवेत्

translations.text: Om is the bow, the self is the arrow, Brahman is said to be the mark. It is to be pierced by one who is heedful; one should become one with it, as the arrow (with the mark).

notes: Śaṅkara: praṇava: the syllable Om is the bow; as a bow makes the arrow enter the mark, so Om makes the self, the arrow, enter the imperishable, the mark; for the self, refined by the repetition of Om and resting on it, settles without hindrance in the imperishable, like an arrow shot from a bow in its mark. śara: the self, which is the supreme itself, entered here into the body, as the sun into water, as the witness of all the cognitions of the intellect, and marked by the adjuncts; like an arrow it is laid on the imperishable Brahman, its own Self. Brahman is called the mark because those who wish to fix the mind aim at it as their own self.

Śaṅkara: apramattena: by one free of the heedlessness that is thirst for outward objects, turned away from everything, master of the senses, with a one-pointed mind, Brahman the mark is to be pierced. tanmayaḥ: after the piercing, as the arrow becomes one with the mark, so one should bring about oneness with the imperishable, setting aside the notion that the body and the rest are the self.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्मिन्द्यौः पृथिवी चान्तरिक्षमोतं मनः सह प्राणैश्च सर्वैः ।
तमेवैकं जानथ आत्मानमन्या वाचो विमुञ्चथामृतस्यैष सेतुः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yasmin dyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣam otaṃ manaḥ saha prāṇaiś ca sarvaiḥ |
tam evaikaṃ jānatha ātmānam anyā vāco vimuñcathāmṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: yasmin dyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣam otaṃ manaḥ saha prāṇaiś ca sarvaiḥ
lines.deva: यस्मिन्द्यौः पृथिवी चान्तरिक्षमोतं मनः सह प्राणैश्च सर्वैः

lines.iast: tam evaikaṃ jānatha ātmānam anyā vāco vimuñcathāmṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ
lines.deva: तमेवैकं जानथ आत्मानमन्या वाचो विमुञ्चथामृतस्यैष सेतुः

padaccheda.iast: yasmin dyauḥ pṛthivī ca antarikṣam otam manaḥ saha prāṇaiḥ ca sarvaiḥ tam eva ekam jānatha ātmānam anyāḥ vācaḥ vimuñcatha amṛtasya eṣaḥ setuḥ
padaccheda.deva: यस्मिन् द्यौः पृथिवी च अन्तरिक्षम् ओतम् मनः सह प्राणैः च सर्वैः तम् एव एकम् जानथ आत्मानम् अन्याः वाचः विमुञ्चथ अमृतस्य एषः सेतुः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Him in whom heaven, earth and the mid-region are woven, and the mind with all the prāṇas (the senses), know him alone as the one Self; give up other words: this is the bridge to immortality.

notes: Śaṅkara: because the imperishable is hard to mark, it is spoken of again and again, so that it may be well marked. Know, pupils, him alone, the ground of all, one without a second, as the inner Self of you and of all beings; and having known him give up the other words, those of the lower knowledge, and all the rites they make known, with their means. setu: this knowledge of the Self is a bridge for reaching immortality, liberation, being the means of crossing the great ocean of the round of birth and death (‘knowing him alone one goes beyond death; there is no other path for going’, Śvetāśvatara 3.8).

sanskrit.deva:
अरा इव रथनाभौ संहता यत्र नाड्यः स एषोऽन्तश्चरते बहुधा जायमानः ।
ओमित्येवं ध्यायथ आत्मानं स्वस्ति वः पाराय तमसः परस्तात् ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
arā iva rathanābhau saṃhatā yatra nāḍyaḥ sa eṣo 'ntaś carate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ |
om ity evaṃ dhyāyatha ātmānaṃ svasti vaḥ pārāya tamasaḥ parastāt || 6 ||

lines.iast: arā iva rathanābhau saṃhatā yatra nāḍyaḥ sa eṣo 'ntaś carate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ
lines.deva: अरा इव रथनाभौ संहता यत्र नाड्यः स एषोऽन्तश्चरते बहुधा जायमानः

lines.iast: om ity evaṃ dhyāyatha ātmānaṃ svasti vaḥ pārāya tamasaḥ parastāt
lines.deva: ओमित्येवं ध्यायथ आत्मानं स्वस्ति वः पाराय तमसः परस्तात्

padaccheda.iast: arāḥ iva ratha-nābhau saṃhatāḥ yatra nāḍyaḥ saḥ eṣaḥ antaḥ carate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ om iti evam dhyāyatha ātmānam svasti vaḥ pārāya tamasaḥ parastāt
padaccheda.deva: अराः इव रथ-नाभौ संहताः यत्र नाड्यः सः एषः अन्तः चरते बहुधा जायमानः ॐ इति एवम् ध्यायथ आत्मानम् स्वस्ति वः पाराय तमसः परस्तात्

words.meaning: in the hub of a chariot wheel

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. pl.

translations.text: Where the channels meet like spokes in the hub of a wheel, there he moves within, born, as it were, in many ways. Meditate on the Self thus, as Om. May it go well with you in reaching the far shore beyond darkness.

notes: Śaṅkara: in the heart, where the channels spreading through the whole body meet like spokes set in the hub of a wheel, this Self, the witness of the cognitions of the intellect, moves within, seeing, hearing, thinking, knowing; born as it were in many ways through cognitions of anger, joy and the like, since it follows the inner organ, its adjunct; people say ‘he has become glad, he has become angry’. Meditate on that Self as Om, resting on the syllable Om in the way described. The teacher who knows must tell his pupils what is to be told; and the pupils, wishing to know Brahman, have given up rites and set out on the path of liberation; so the teacher blesses them, that they may reach Brahman without hindrance: may it go well with you in reaching the far shore beyond the darkness of ignorance, that is, in going to the nature of Brahman, the Self, free of ignorance.

sanskrit.deva:
यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्यैष महिमा भुवि ।
दिव्ये ब्रह्मपुरे ह्येष व्योम्न्यात्मा प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavid yasyaiṣa mahimā bhuvi |
divye brahmapure hy eṣa vyomny ātmā pratiṣṭhitaḥ || 7 ||

lines.iast: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavid yasyaiṣa mahimā bhuvi
divye brahmapure hy eṣa vyomny ātmā pratiṣṭhitaḥ

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit yasya eṣaḥ mahimā bhuvi divye brahma-pure hi eṣaḥ vyomni ātmā pratiṣṭhitaḥ
padaccheda.deva: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्ववित् यस्य एषः महिमा भुवि दिव्ये ब्रह्म-पुरे हि एषः व्योम्नि आत्मा प्रतिष्ठितः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: He who is all-knowing and knows each thing, whose is this greatness in the world: this Self is established (as it were) in the space within the shining city of Brahman (the heart).

notes: Śaṅkara: where is he who, beyond the darkness, is to be reached by crossing the ocean of the round? sarvajñaḥ sarvavit: as explained (1.1.9). mahimā: his well-known glory: by whose command heaven and earth stand held apart; by whose command the sun and moon wheel ceaselessly like a fire-brand; by whose command rivers and seas do not pass their bounds; under whose command the moving and unmoving are ruled; whose command the seasons, the half-years and the years do not transgress; by whose command agents, acts and fruits do not pass their times. divye brahmapure: in the shining city of Brahman, lit by all the cognitions of the intellect, for Brahman is ever manifest there as consciousness; the city of Brahman is the lotus of the heart; in the space within it he is perceived as if established there; for one who pervades all like space there is no other going, coming or abiding.

This and the next mantra (yaḥ sarvajñaḥ … pratiṣṭhitaḥ; manomayaḥ … vibhāti) are numbered 7 and 8 in the edition, as in the bhāṣya; some editions print them as one mantra, giving eleven for this khaṇḍa.

sanskrit.deva:
मनोमयः प्राणशरीरनेता प्रतिष्ठितोऽन्ने हृदयं संनिधाय ।
तद्विज्ञानेन परिपश्यन्ति धीरा आनन्दरूपममृतं यद्विभाति ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīranetā pratiṣṭhito 'nne hṛdayaṃ saṃnidhāya |
tad vijñānena paripaśyanti dhīrā ānandarūpam amṛtaṃ yad vibhāti || 8 ||

lines.iast: manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīranetā pratiṣṭhito 'nne hṛdayaṃ saṃnidhāya
tad vijñānena paripaśyanti dhīrā ānandarūpam amṛtaṃ yad vibhāti

padaccheda.iast: manomayaḥ prāṇa-śarīra-netā pratiṣṭhitaḥ anne hṛdayam saṃnidhāya tat vijñānena paripaśyanti dhīrāḥ ānanda-rūpam amṛtam yat vibhāti
padaccheda.deva: मनोमयः प्राण-शरीर-नेता प्रतिष्ठितः अन्ने हृदयम् संनिधाय तत् विज्ञानेन परिपश्यन्ति धीराः आनन्द-रूपम् अमृतम् यत् विभाति

words.meaning: the leader of prāṇa and the body

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Consisting of mind, the leader of prāṇa and the (subtle) body, he is established in food (the gross body), having placed the understanding (in the heart). By knowledge the wise see fully that which shines as bliss, immortal.

notes: Śaṅkara: manomayaḥ: the Self dwelling there is known only through the activities of the mind, its adjunct. prāṇaśarīranetā: the leader of prāṇa and of that body, who leads it from this gross body to another, subtle one. pratiṣṭhito 'nne: abiding in food, the bodily mass made of the food that is eaten, growing and wasting day by day, having placed the heart, the intellect, in the opening of the lotus; for the Self abides by the intellect abiding in the heart, not by itself in food. vijñānena: by the special knowledge born of the teaching of scripture and teacher, and arising from calm, restraint, meditation, the renouncing of all, and dispassion, the discerning see that principle of the Self full on every side: of the nature of bliss, free of all evil, sorrow and toil, immortal, shining always in their own Self.

sanskrit.deva:
भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः ।
क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhidyate hṛdayagranthiś chidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ |
kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare || 9 ||

lines.iast: bhidyate hṛdayagranthiś chidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ
kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare

padaccheda.iast: bhidyate hṛdaya-granthiḥ chidyante sarva-saṃśayāḥ kṣīyante ca asya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare
padaccheda.deva: भिद्यते हृदय-ग्रन्थिः छिद्यन्ते सर्व-संशयाः क्षीयन्ते च अस्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्टे परावरे

grammar.en: past passive participle m. loc. sg.

translations.text: The knot of the heart is cut, all doubts are severed, and his actions are exhausted, when he is seen who is both the high and the low.

notes: Śaṅkara: this is the fruit of the knowledge of the supreme Self. hṛdayagranthi: desire, made of the impressions of ignorance and resting in the intellect (‘the desires that rest in his heart’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.7); it rests in the heart, not in the Self. All doubts about what is to be known, which in worldly people flow on like the stream of the Gaṅgā until death, are cut off. Of him whose doubts are cut and whose ignorance has ceased, the actions done before knowledge arose, in this and other births, whose fruits have not begun, and those done together with the rise of knowledge, are exhausted; not those that began this birth, for their fruit has already begun. parāvara: high as the cause, low as the effect; when he is seen directly as ‘I am he’, one is freed, the cause of the round being cut off.

sanskrit.deva:
हिरण्मये परे कोशे विरजं ब्रह्म निष्कलम् ।
तच्छुभ्रं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिस्तद्यदात्मविदो विदुः ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
hiraṇmaye pare kośe virajaṃ brahma niṣkalam |
tac chubhraṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotis tad yad ātmavido viduḥ || 10 ||

lines.iast: hiraṇmaye pare kośe virajaṃ brahma niṣkalam
lines.deva: हिरण्मये परे कोशे विरजं ब्रह्म निष्कलम्

lines.iast: tac chubhraṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotis tad yad ātmavido viduḥ

padaccheda.iast: hiraṇmaye pare kośe virajam brahma niṣkalam tat śubhram jyotiṣām jyotiḥ tat yat ātma-vidaḥ viduḥ
padaccheda.deva: हिरण्मये परे कोशे विरजम् ब्रह्म निष्कलम् तत् शुभ्रम् ज्योतिषाम् ज्योतिः तत् यत् आत्म-विदः विदुः

translations.text: In the highest golden sheath (the light of the understanding) is the stainless Brahman, without parts. It is pure, the light of lights; it is what the knowers of the Self know.

notes: Śaṅkara: this and the next two mantras sum up what has been said. hiraṇmaye: shining, the light of the knowing of the intellect; kośe: a sheath, as of a sword, being the place where the nature of the Self is realized; pare: highest, being innermost of all. virajam: free of the dust and stain of ignorance and every other fault; brahma: being greatest and the Self of all; niṣkalam: from which all parts have gone, partless. jyotiṣāṃ jyotiḥ: the light even of fire and the other lights; their being lights is owed to the light of consciousness of Brahman, the Self within them; that is the supreme light, the light of the Self, which no other lights. ātmavidaḥ: the discerning who know their own Self as the witness of the cognitions of sound and other objects know it, following the inward cognition; not others, who follow outward things.

sanskrit.deva:
न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः ।
तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yam agniḥ |
tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti || 11 ||

lines.iast: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yam agniḥ
lines.deva: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः

lines.iast: tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti
lines.deva: तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति

padaccheda.iast: na tatra sūryaḥ bhāti na candra-tārakam na imāḥ vidyutaḥ bhānti kutaḥ ayam agniḥ tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvam tasya bhāsā sarvam idam vibhāti
padaccheda.deva: न तत्र सूर्यः भाति न चन्द्र-तारकम् न इमाः विद्युतः भान्ति कुतः अयम् अग्निः तम् एव भान्तम् अनुभाति सर्वम् तस्य भासा सर्वम् इदम् विभाति

translations.text: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars; these lightnings do not shine; how then this fire? Everything shines after him alone as he shines; by his light all this shines.

notes: Śaṅkara: how it is the light of lights: in Brahman, his own Self, the sun, though it lights all, does not shine, that is, does not light Brahman; for it lights all else, the not-self, by Brahman's light, and has no power of its own to light it. So with the moon and stars and lightning; how then this fire within our reach? All this world that shines shines after the supreme Lord, who shines, being light by nature; as water or a firebrand burns after the fire that burns, by contact with it, not of itself. Since Brahman shines and shines variously through the varied light in its effects, its being light by nature is known; what has no light of its own cannot give light to another: pots and the like are not seen to light others, but the sun and other luminous things are.

sanskrit.deva:
ब्रह्मैवेदममृतं पुरस्ताद्ब्रह्म पश्चाद्ब्रह्म दक्षिणतश्चोत्तरेण ।
अधश्चोर्ध्वं च प्रसृतं ब्रह्मैवेदं विश्वमिदं वरिष्ठम् ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
brahmaivedam amṛtaṃ purastād brahma paścād brahma dakṣiṇataś cottareṇa |
adhaś cordhvaṃ ca prasṛtaṃ brahmaivedaṃ viśvam idaṃ variṣṭham || 12 ||

lines.iast: brahmaivedam amṛtaṃ purastād brahma paścād brahma dakṣiṇataś cottareṇa
adhaś cordhvaṃ ca prasṛtaṃ brahmaivedaṃ viśvam idaṃ variṣṭham
lines.deva: अधश्चोर्ध्वं च प्रसृतं ब्रह्मैवेदं विश्वमिदं वरिष्ठम्

padaccheda.iast: brahma eva idam amṛtam purastāt brahma paścāt brahma dakṣiṇataḥ ca uttareṇa adhaḥ ca ūrdhvam ca prasṛtam brahma eva idam viśvam idam variṣṭham
padaccheda.deva: ब्रह्म एव इदम् अमृतम् पुरस्तात् ब्रह्म पश्चात् ब्रह्म दक्षिणतः च उत्तरेण अधः च ऊर्ध्वम् च प्रसृतम् ब्रह्म एव इदम् विश्वम् इदम् वरिष्ठम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Brahman alone, the immortal, is this (that appears) in front; Brahman behind, Brahman to the south and to the north; spread out below and above. Brahman alone is this universe, the best.

notes: Śaṅkara: Brahman, the light of lights, alone is true; all else is its modification, a mere name resting on speech, untrue: this, set out at length with reasons, is summed up by this mantra, which stands as the conclusion. What appears in front, as if it were not Brahman, to those whose sight is ignorance, is Brahman alone; so behind, to the south, to the north, below and above: what spreads out everywhere in the form of effects, appearing as if other, with name and form. In a word, this whole world is Brahman alone, the best. Every notion of what is not Brahman is mere ignorance, like the notion of a snake in a rope; Brahman alone, one, is the truth in the highest sense: this is the teaching of the Veda.
